verdicts.rationale: The introduction identifies fine details, small objects, intricate boundaries and uniformly applied refinement as the targeted problems.
The architecture description specifies MAE-pretrained plain ViT, FPN, two click disk-map channels and the previous mask, with prompt embeddings added to image embeddings.
The methods explicitly describe mask-derived edge supervision using differential operators and a weighted combination of normalized focal and Dice losses.
Equations 4–6 define exactly this uncertainty formula and its product with the normalized Sobel contour-gradient magnitude.
The pseudo-click procedure specifies the maximum-uncertainty candidate, inclusive skip interval, strict positive and negative thresholds, and feedback of accepted clicks.
The setup lists all named evaluation datasets and reports the stated SBD training and test image counts.
The out-of-domain evaluation explicitly names these medical and SEM datasets and states SBD-only training without target-domain fine-tuning.
The edge-head ablation reports all three NoC@90 reductions exactly as claimed.
The reported COCO_MVal first-click mIoU and NSDS values match the claim.
Table 2 compares one-step refinement variants and gives the three stated NoC@90 pairs.
The Berkeley comparison reports these values and relative reductions; the percentages agree with the rounded numbers.
The OAIZIB discussion reports all three metric pairs against SimpleClick exactly as stated.
Table 4 gives the stated SEM-Precipitate NoC@85 and NSDS values for the model and SimpleClick.
Table 2 shows lower U-CFR mIoU@10 on all three datasets, with exactly the claimed values.
The methods explicitly characterize the edge head as a training regularizer and acknowledge potential connectivity benefits from topology-aware losses.
The conclusion identifies these two contributions and states that inference-time pseudo-click refinement requires no additional user input.
